issues.description: Normalization only handles ClassName nodes; IDs, attributes, pseudos, and tag selectors with escapes are still false negatives
issues.detail: The fix narrowly targets `parser.isClassName(node)`, but escape-sequence equivalence applies to other selector types too (e.g., `#u-m\00002b` vs `#u-m\+`, `[data-x="\00002b"]`, `:is(...)`, pseudo-class arguments, type selectors). The PR title and changeset are framed broadly as "escaped selectors," but only class selectors are normalized. Either the scope should be expanded (postcss-selector-parser exposes the same getter/setter pattern for Identifier/Tag/Attribute/Pseudo) or the changeset and tests should be narrowed to claim only class-selector coverage.

issues.description: Self-assignment relies on undocumented postcss-selector-parser internals and is fragile
issues.detail: `node.value = node.value` triggers re-escaping only because postcss-selector-parser's ClassName setter happens to overwrite `raws.value`. This is an implementation detail of that library, not a documented API contract. If postcss-selector-parser changes its setter behavior (or adds a fast-path that no-ops on equal assignment), the fix silently regresses. Consider either calling a dedicated normalize API, manually clearing `raws.value`, or adding a regression test that asserts the post-normalization stringification — not just the rule outcome.

issues.description: Changeset is labeled `minor` but this is a bug fix
issues.detail: The changeset declares `"stylelint": minor`, but the PR fixes a false-negative bug in an existing rule. Per typical semver and stylelint's own conventions for rule bug fixes, this should be `patch`. A `minor` bump would only be warranted if this changed documented rule behavior or added new options.

issues.description: Test coverage misses several escape-equivalence cases worth pinning
issues.detail: The reject tests cover hex-vs-character and short-vs-long hex on a class selector. Missing: trailing-space-terminated hex (`\2b ` vs `\2b`), uppercase vs lowercase hex (`\2B` vs `\2b`), and mixed-case selectors that previously normalized via other paths. Adding a couple of these would lock in the contract this PR is asserting and would also surface the type-selector/ID gap noted above.

issues.description: `@ts-expect-error` swallows a real typing gap rather than fixing it
issues.detail: The `raws.value` access is suppressed via `@ts-expect-error` with a comment about performance. Since `raws` is a real (if undocumented) property on selector nodes, the cleaner fix is to declare a narrow local type or augment the import — `@ts-expect-error` will silently break if upstream types are updated to include `raws`, masking unrelated type regressions.

issues.description: Helper is called twice per node via both the explicit call and the walk callback
issues.detail: `normalizeSelector` calls `normalizeNodeEscaping(node)` directly, then `node.walk(...)` will visit the same node's descendants but also re-walk in a pattern that mirrors the existing whitespace normalization. This matches the pre-existing structure, so it's not a regression — but it's worth confirming `walk` does not include the root node itself; if it ever did, double-normalization on classes is harmless but wasteful given the `raws.value` short-circuit. A brief comment clarifying the intentional root-then-descendants pattern would help future readers.

dissents.topic: Scope of normalization: classes-only vs all selector types

positions.position: Ship the class-only fix now — it resolves the filed issue (#3972) with a small, surgical change and minimal risk. Other selector types can be addressed in a follow-up when there's a concrete bug report.

The bug is fundamentally about escape-sequence equivalence; gating on `isClassName` encodes the wrong abstraction boundary. The normalization helper should iterate over all node types that expose value getter/setter normalization, or the PR should be honestly scoped (title, changeset, tests) to class selectors only.

This depends on an undocumented side effect in a third-party library's setter. The behavior should either be guaranteed by a contract test against postcss-selector-parser or replaced with an explicit `delete node.raws.value` to make the intent legible.

The PR links the exact upstream source lines that guarantee the behavior, adds a no-self-assign eslint suppression with a clear comment, and the test suite locks in the observable outcome. That's sufficient documentation and regression protection.
Bug fixes to existing rules are `patch` by convention. Calling this `minor` inflates the release significance and may confuse downstream consumers tracking changelogs.

stylelint historically treats new rule behavior — even bug-fix-shaped — as `minor` because it can newly flag previously-passing CSS. Under that lens, `minor` is correct because users may see new warnings after upgrading.

review.summary: The fix is small, well-motivated, and includes targeted tests that prove the reported bug is resolved. The core concerns are scope and durability: normalization is gated to ClassName only, leaving IDs, attributes, type selectors, and pseudos with the same latent false negatives despite the PR's broader framing. The mechanism — `node.value = node.value` to trigger the library's setter — is clever but depends on undocumented postcss-selector-parser internals, so a regression test against the stringification (not just the rule's warning output) would harden it. The `minor` changeset bump is debatable under stylelint's conventions but worth confirming. Recommend addressing the scope/title mismatch and tightening the typing suppression before merge; no P0 blockers.
